text_fidelity_a:
Avantree DG40SA Dedicated Windows 10 Bluetooth USB Adapter, Wireless Dongle for PC Bought with Win 10, Plug & Play, Support Headpones, PS4 Gaming Controllers, Mouse, Keyboard, Printers etc. I purchased a Lenovo Ideacentre AIO Y910 in December 2017 and it had a beautiful built-in Qualcomm bluetooth function. It worked great. I had my desktop paired with my Echo Dots and with Alexa could continue listening to movies/music/podcasts/youtube anywhere in my house away from the computer. Along came a Windows 10 update in March 2018 that disabled/removed the bluetooth function/drivers ENTIRELY. No roll backs/restores, or reinstallations brought it back. The internal bluetooth function was completely ruined and prevented from running. I was furious and microsoft support was zero help. I finally begrudgingly purchased this to do the same function. I'm angry I had to pay for something I already paid for my computer to have, and that I have to waste a USB spot for it, but it works, was truly plug and play, though the connecting of all my speakers/Echo Dots is more complicated that previously. For example, with the original bluetooth capabilities, I could chose to have one or both of the Dots automatically connect when bluetooth was enabled. I could have them play together or verbally tell Alexa to connect/disconnect. Now for some reason with this bluetooth, voice control doesn't work, Alexa can't disconnect (she will do it but then it automatically reconnects) and if one Dot is connected the other won't. I have to run back to my computer's bluetooth settings and pair/unpair and connect/disconnect each time I want to make a change. This is frustrating. If anyone knows of anyway to circumvent this or the original bluetooth death please let me know, I'd be forever grateful.

The range for the device is fine, I live in a 1200 sq ft two story townhome and there was no issue with my computer seeing the Dot in the bedroom or the Dot downstairs. Connections are strong.
text_fidelity_b: Avantree DG40SA Dedicated Windows 10 Bluetooth USB Adapter, Wireless Dongle for PC Bought with Win 10, Plug & Play, Support Headpones, PS4 Gaming Controllers, Mouse, Keyboard, Printers etc.

text_fidelity_a:
D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D) This will tell you if a battery is good or bad. However since it has no internal power source, it uses the power of the battery you are testing to give you a reading. This requires a power drain on the battery you are testing, which will ALWAYS give you inaccurate results. If you take a very small battery, such as a 1.5 V watch battery that is 1/3 depleted, this may be as mush as 30% off on the low side. Example, I checked a 1.5 V watch batty and this showed 1.0 V. Using a high end, self powered volt meter, the battery shoed 1.4V. That is a huge difference.

So again, it will show you a dead battery, but so will dropping a battery on end on a hard surface, If it bounces its dead, if it thuds and does not bounce, its good. Work on all AA, AAA, C, D. batteries.
text_fidelity_b: D-FantiX Digital Battery Tester, Universal Battery Checker Household Battery Testers for AAA AA C D 9V 1.5V Small Batteries Button Cell (Model: BT-168D)

text_fidelity_a:
WD My Book Live 2TB Personal Cloud Storage NAS Share Files and Photos I just got My Book Live yesterday. I really wanted just a plain old back up, but having an Electronics Engineering degree, I had to stay current. I can't really complain at this point, because I am backing up an 11 year old computer that is slowing to a crawl anyhow. It did not take long to set this drive up on my network. All of my devices immediately found it on the network and play music from the MBL. I had my Kindle HD out in the yard, playing music right off of MBL, while I do my gardening (downloaded the free app for Kindle). It was cool. I feel it will probably be short lived. Last year I bought a cheap WiFi receiver and it was so fast, this year it is so slow. I don't have high expectations from WiFi, and this drive only has the capability to plug into the network. It does not have USB connectivity at all. I do often times want a quick and easy way to transfer files to my new computer, while I do other things. The price was not too bad, but for that money I hope to be able to recover my data even after the WiFi dies. A good back up drive from WD usually last for years. That is what customers are accustomed to anyhow. I will probably update this review in one year. I did password protect my drive before the first file ever got added. I did update the firmware also. So far it is a nice thing to have.
My update on this drive is that it gets better as I use it. I don't know why that new things on my network start out slow and speed up as they are used, but it is working well.
text_fidelity_b: WD My Book Live 2TB Personal Cloud Storage NAS Share Files and Photos

text_fidelity_a:
Canon PowerShot SD1100IS 8MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Blue) (OLD MODEL) This is a solid little camera that can provide excellent image quality under the right conditions. But it has two glaring deficiencies:

1. No fill flash option in auto mode. (There is a fill flash option in manual mode, but it's not easy for the casual user to find.) There's red-eye reduction, of course, and you can turn the flash off completely or let the camera decide when to fire it. But with the camera in auto mode, you can't tell it to fire the flash on every shot, regardless of what its sensor thinks. Major bummer when you want to photograph a backlit subject.

2. Shot-to-shot time is agonizingly slow, and focus time isn't especially speedy, either. This is a problem when, for example, you want to catch quick snaps of the animals you see on Disney World's Kilimanjaro Safaris. Ask me how I know.

I'm sure this is a fine camera for people who want to photograph landscapes, still lifes, and posed portraits. For candid shots of subjects in motion, it's not so great.
text_fidelity_b: Canon PowerShot SD1100IS 8MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Image Stabilized Zoom (Blue) (OLD MODEL)

text_fidelity_a:
HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA) I got my first PC in 2003, and had a corded mouse. Looking back, I can BARELY remember the mouse that came with that Gateway PC. In 2004, my mom bought a Dell PC and traded me for my Gateway – don’t judge, she just wanted something to browse the internet and play games on.

Between 2003-2005, I used an awkward racecar shaped mouse, but went back to the more streamlined corded mouse for my desktops.

In 2005, when I got a laptop, I got my first wireless mouse and liked it. It was a Logitech.

By 2010, I got my first HP laptop – and as usual, got a specific mouse for it, again Logitech. The reason? My hand. I don’t have very big hands and hate to “splay” my fingers out trying to grip the mouse. That continued with a backup laptop in 2011 with some college money.

I even got “backup” mice, I just LOVED the Logitech ones.

Last year, 2021, I got another HP laptop for my birthday and yes – a “Logi” mouse (M317 – Amazon code B08L8SRJRR; white with purple/pink side grip, flowers on top). This was a bit smaller than my previous mice. But, I love it.

Thinking this might be a bit better – I got it.

Right off – it is a bit “extra”. I can BARELY grip it to get it to do what I need to do. The “thumb” rest was a good idea, the USB rechargeable feature was nice, programmable buttons – a bit beyond me. This is definitely for someone who needs those features.

As far as “quiet” with regards to the scrolling and clicking – I don’t see the need for the feature. When I’m typing on they keyboard that is noisier than my mouse.

It was response and fast – but not enough to justify a purchase of it.

It connects the same way my “Logi” does – USB dongle. Both mice take ONE (1) AA battery

At the current price of $67.52 – this is a definitely no-go for me.
text_fidelity_b: HP 970 Programmable Wireless Keyboard (Silver) - Bluetooth & 2.4 GHz Wireless Multi-Device Connectivity - USB-C Rechargeable Battery - 24 Programmable Keys - Works with Windows & MacOS (3Z729AA#ABA)

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.

text_fidelity_a:
K&F Concept 49mm UV CPL Lens Filter Kit 18 Multi Layer Coatings Circular Polarizer Filter & MC UV Protection Filter Set for Camera Lens K-Series [[VIDEOID:2b8bb26ef242fcb874bd3c461ac0e558]] For the price, this is a decent circular polarizing filter for amateurs who want to get into using a polarizing filter. It includes a UV filter that I consider just an extra.

I personally don't recommend the use of UV filters unless you are shooting film, as they generally don't improve image quality on modern digital cameras and, if anything, can only degrade it. I know that a lot of people consider them a layer of protection for their expensive lenses, but I am of the opinion that having a cheap UV filter on your expensive lens is actually more likely to damage it. Case in point, the threads on this filter are very sharply cut. You can feel and hear them grinding when you screw it into place, and when it is tightened down snug, the sharp threads want to lock it into place. If the lens was knocked hard on the corner with the filter in this position, the UV filter might actually become stuck in place and damage the threads of the lens, requiring expert repairs to remove the filter and repair the lens. In my experience, just keeping the lens hood in place offers far more protection than a UV filter possibly could.

With that out of the way, let's get to the meat of this review, which is the CPL filter. For the price, this will perform perfectly well. It will darken the sky when used properly in the right conditions, and can help reduce glare and reflections. It seems to have no discernible color cast which would be a problem. In fact the only real issue I have with this filter is related to the mechanical function.

First of all, the threads are very sharply cut, as mentioned previously with the UV filter. This isn't the end of the world, but it is coupled by the fact that the rotating ring on the CPL filter is also very, very stiff and resists turning quite a lot. In order to turn it, as is necessary for adjusting it to the present conditions, you will need to tighten the filter down onto your lens more than I would like, and with such sharp threads, this increases the risk of the threads locking firmly onto your lens. It is possible for them to lock so firmly that it could be quite difficult to remove it from your lens. While $30 is a pretty good bargain for what is otherwise a pretty decent filter, it's not such a bargain if it runs the risk of costing you a lot of money in repairs to your expensive gear. If you are using a cheap lens, then this cheap filter should be just fine. If you have shelled out lots of money for an expensive lens, I would not recommend cheaping out on the filters.

In the end I settled on 4 stars because the glass is pretty decent quality, and if you are aware of the limitations you can safely use it so long as you avoid tightening it down too much. It's just a little less convenient. But it otherwise works well.
text_fidelity_b: K&F Concept 49mm UV CPL Lens Filter Kit 18 Multi Layer Coatings Circular Polarizer Filter & MC UV Protection Filter Set for Camera Lens K-Series

text_fidelity_a:
Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit In terms of installation, it really doesn't get any easier: basically just plug in the control module and tap a couple buttons to register each camera and you're in business. Took me all of 5 minutes.

The cameras themselves aren't feature rich - you're not going to find tilt/swivel/zoom or even night vision. But you can't expect it from cameras that operate in 2 AA for up to 2 years! They do what they're designed to do: basic monitoring with motion detection in a completely wireless setup (you can literally place the cameras anywhere!). An LED light can illuminate any recording in darkness.

There's no monthly service fee either - but the recordings you can take are only up to a minute long and there's a limit on how many.

I love these cameras for their ease of setup and complete mobility. The only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars is the lack of an outdoor camera option and a little bit buggy iOS app.

Update (11/27/2017): a couple negatives to the cameras:
(1) while each camera comes with a wall mount, orienting it just right (in my case on a front porch so I could see who's at the door) isn't all that easy (just because the camera doesn't have an area in its view doesn't mean it won't detect motion slightly outside it!)
(2) the cameras have no speakers. I knew this when buying, of course, but competing cameras in same price range do.
(3) I just asked Blink whether there are any plans for Apple HomeKIt support - and there aren't :-( This is a big negative for me because I'm starting to do some home automation and since we're an Apple household, I want HomeKit. So I'm going to be looking for another set of cameras instead of expanding my Blink set :-(
text_fidelity_b: Blink Indoor Home Security Camera System with Motion Detection, HD Video, 2-Year Battery Life and Cloud Storage Included - 3 Camera Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher Price Precious Planet Whale of a Tub We purchased this product before we were expecting, knowing that it was neutral gendered and would be perfect for a boy or a girl. When we had our first child, a 9 lb, 11 oz baby girl, I was SO nervous! I didn't know a thing about babies. My eldest sister helped me give her her first bath and complimented our whale tub. She said it was so nice that the green padding in the base would help prevent baby from slipping. By the third bath, I had it down.

As the weeks have gone on, our little one has really loved her tub. She began holding her head up at 4 days old and was doing so independently within a month of her birth. She loved kicking and splashing in her tub. She has never cried in the bath. We use a turtlemeter thermometer and she thinks of it like a little toy with which to play.

I would recommend this tub with the seat in it for a newborn baby up to about 12 lbs. Once our daughter was 13 lbs, she has trouble staying warm in the tub with the seat attached. It simply wasn't deep enough for her while she was lying down and she only got her bottom half wet unless I poured water over her, and the chilly air would then make her cold.

With the seat out, she needs to be sitting on her own so there was a two month gap where we did not use her tub, and instead bathed her with me in the big tub.

Once she was a successful sitter, we returned her to this tub for warmer nights, so she could sit and play in the water. She loves it!

After a bath, I would recommend not only using the drain in the tub, but turning this whale tub upside-down and and then turning it from side-to-side to drain it, as the water tends to get trapped beneath the green padded area. You can also remove the seat to clean under it. Using dish soap and a scrub daddy sponge, I am able to quickly clean the tub in-between uses.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher Price Precious Planet Whale of a Tub

So they must have made some useful advances in the relevant technology in the four years since I last purchased a transmitter from them.

I have tested this transmitter with multiple Bluetooth headphones that I own, and in each case, the Bluetooth connects seamlessly. I like the fact that the transmitter speaks and lets me know when the Bluetooth has connected. And a split second after that, the sound from my TV comes through my Bluetooth headphones. My old Avantree transmitter had neither of those abilities. It would take up to 2 minutes to get it connected to my Bluetooth headphones after multiple tries, and the sound's clarity and volume weren't nearly as good.

As was the case with my previous transmitter, this one can handle multiple Bluetooth headphones at the same time. So far I have only attempted transmission with two at a time.

Finally, the appearance of this transmitter is much fancier than the old one. I will admit that it is about three times larger than the old one, but that is not really a problem for me, because the old one was tiny and this one is still conveniently small. It has some cute, space-age looking little antennas on it that the other one didn't have, which may partially account for why it works so much better.

All in all, I am very pleased with this purchase.

Bose Portable Home Speaker with Alexa Voice Control Built-in Portable Home Speaker Charging Cradle, Black This is a great speaker! It has great Bose sound and gets loud!!!!
The speaker is very well packaged.
The cable has the same usbc plug in both sides. I will be buying the additional dock unit so I can just grab and go and not have to unplug it every time I want to take it somewhere.
The speaker requires the Bose Music app.
There isn’t much instructions that come with the actual speaker - it’s all online.
I already have the Bose Music app and was hoping I could just use all the settings I have already set up for another speaker - but it didn’t let me do that.
The actual setup process took me about 20 minutes.
The touch pad is very responsive and the voice pickup is great!
I don’t have to yell at it like some of my other devices!
The presets are available on the app and are pretty easy to setup. I set them up using both Amazon Music and Pandora.
In the Alexa app the Bose speaker is found under the Echo & Alexa group. It’s currently not able to be added to a speaker group as it’s treated more like a speaker than an Alexa. Hopefully an app update will change to allow this.
I also have a Bose Revolve (original) and Bose Home Speaker 300.
I am able to sync this speaker and the Home Speaker 300 through Apple Airplay 2 and the Bose Music app but this hasn’t been possible through the Alexa app.
This portable speaker has the same great sound as my Home 300 speaker. When they are playing next to each other they are in sync and make for great whole house sound.
Overall this is a great speaker with great sound and Alexa works perfectly! The setup was pretty minimal and it’s easy to use.
I like this speaker over my original Bose Revolve as I like the handle and I like to be able to tell Alexa to do things while I’m outside.
One issue I have is really with the app. I can’t seem to change the WiFi connection to the speaker without deleting the speaker from the Bose Music app.
I can change the name but not the WiFi.
I feel like I should be able to carry this speaker anywhere and connect to a friend’s WiFi or the WiFi of a guest house easily. The current way the software is set up, that’s not possible. I’m hoping there will be a software update in the future to fix this. Until then I’ll just have to use Bluetooth at those locations.
This was a little disappointing but nothing I can’t work around and doesn’t change the greatness of this speaker.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Portable Home Speaker with Alexa Voice Control Built-in Portable Home Speaker Charging Cradle, Black

Sangean PR-D7 BK AM/FM Digital Rechargeable Portable Radio - Black (PR-D7BK) I like this radio for AM reception. Comes with an AC adapter that also charges the six nickel metal hydride (NiMH) AA cells if you buy and install them. You must throw a little switch (one time process) to tell the radio which type of cells are installed (regular or rechargeable) so the radio doesn't try to recharge the non-rechargeable cells.

One flaw is that it does not have a handle for convenient carrying. It is portable, after all. It's not that you can't carry it, but it's not very "grippable" and a handle is way better. I bought one of these radios for my 90-yr old dad, who was grabbing it by the buttons and accidentally reprogramming it. The handle assures it stays set properly and won't be accidentally dropped.

I epoxied an auxiliary handle on, as you can see in the photo. The handle is simple white plastic door pull left over from a prefab storage cabinet. Seems to stick fine using two-part 5-minute epoxy adhesive.

One other nit is that the volume control knob is very easy to adjust. I'd like it to have a bit more resistance so it stays at a set volume.

text_fidelity_a:
adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches I wear headphones when I work outside, spring through fall. By the end of fall, that year’s pair is pretty nasty from hours of daily use and me sweating in them. Of course I clean them, but it’s impossible to *really* deep clean headphones.

So that’s what drew me to the adidas RPT-01 Sport Headphones: the description advertises “removable, washable knitted ear cushions.” Knit covers I can wash? Hooray!

But there’s no instructions in the box on how to remove the ear covers or the headband. It turns out the cushions aren’t as removable as advertised.The ear cups twist off the headphones (a gentle, counter-clockwise turn), but there’s still an inner plastic rim. I thought I’d be able to wash the knitted cover itself, but nope. And I nearly tore the cover trying to figure out how to remove it, until I found the manual online.

I can’t figure out how to get the headband all the way off. The black plastic lining is removable, allowing the headband to be pushed up. I worry the headband will tear quickly, as the holes that line up with the black plastic lining aren’t reinforced.

Sound quality is okay … as long as I don’t use the Control Knob.

The Control Knob is like a volume rocker and skip/go back button in one. But when I used it to change the volume and skip tracks, I had static that lasted for several seconds.

There is an adidas Headphones app, but I thought it was useless. The only advantage of the app is that it allows you to set up to 3 customizable actions for the other button on the headphones. Oddly enough, at the time of writing this review, the app was only available on Android. I wanted to test the headphones on an iPhone too, but could not because the adidas Headphones app wasn’t available in my country (USA).

Lastly, the headphones are so uncomfortable to wear that I can’t wear them for more than 10 minutes. If I were inclined to use them, which I’m not, mainly because of the static whenever I use the Control Knob. I have a small head, but these headphones are tight and squeeze my ears and head. The ear cushions are actually quite scratchy too.
text_fidelity_b: adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - Night Grey, 2.8 x 5.6 x 7.5 Inches

text_fidelity_a:
Canon Cameras US PowerShot SX720 HS Black My SX280 HS is becoming unreliable, throwing E32 lens errors. This is the closest replacement, AFAIK. The 40x zoom is probably not that useful, since the 280's 20x was right at the limit of stable framing, but no biggie. I just like the SX HS series with the DIGIC 6 processor. I looked at the 730, but didn't need Bluetooth & didn't like the look of the oversimplified controls. And $50 buys a couple of extra batteries.

One thing you do get for several years of technology development is a better battery/sensor. Thus far the 720 shows no sign of gobbling electricity the way the 280 does. The extra $100 also buys a better written manual. I discovered a couple of minor features both cameras have, but which you'd be hard pressed to figure out from the 280's manual.--9/2/2017
Update: The 280's video/battery life problems are fixed in the 720. Image stabilization is very good. I got acceptable results at >20x zoom with a light-weight monopod (a Slik). Close focus also appears much better.--9/4/2017
I'm still on my first battery charge!--9/17/2017
Update: I fixed the 280's lens errors with a can of air and a heavy hand blowing out the gaps in the lens. Risky, but it worked. The 720 is still my go to camera. I upped the rating to 5.
July 2019 Update--I got a killer deal on a Panasonic Lumix ZS70. Great camera ... but ... it feels a lot bigger than this one in my hand. It has more features, does more things, but the 720 is lighter, handier, and in some cases takes better still pictures. If you don't need an EVF, tilt-screen and better video, this (or its SX740HS successor) might just be the better choice. The 740 has a tilt-screen.
June 2020
One word of advice. The sensor is 20 Mpx. The lens is capable of delivering 5-8 Mpx. This is typical of these small cameras. Don't be afraid to use lower resolutions or higher compressions. You won't lose much. Still a favorite camera.
text_fidelity_b: Canon Cameras US PowerShot SX720 HS Black

HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 GB Solid-State Drive, Windows 10 Home (14-cd1042nr, Mineral Silver) It's not hyperbole for me to say I love this laptop. After working with glitchy, draggy old computers for the last year or so, this is a huge revelation for me. Not only is it fast on a task-to-task basis, but the startup and shutdown processes are incredibly fast. It's not wasting my time. Nor does it waste my time with a lot of bloatware. Yes there is some, but most is easy to remove should you not want it.

I like a smaller screen and keyboard, so this is perfect for me, and it's lightweight and has a slim profile, so it's easy to take along when I'm out and about. I love the way it converts to a tablet when you fold the screen back. Even the fingerprint recognition is dramatically better than anything I've had before. One thing I was skeptical about was the placement of the power button on the side. I was sure I'd be turning the laptop on or off accidentally, but I've discovered that it's not that simple, which is a load off my mind.

I could wish for a couple more USB ports particularly as I use both a wireless mouse and because there's no disk drive, so I have to attach an external one when I want to access files on disk. Eh, I'll survive it. There are always work-arounds.

Bottom line is that this laptop is a perfect match for me. I'm a writer (not a gamer) and this runs all the software I need, runs it fast and efficiently, and has tremendous storage capacity for all my files. I really couldn't have asked for more. Nicely done, HP.
text_fidelity_b: HP Pavilion X360 14-Inch Convertible Laptop, Intel Core I5-8265U Processor, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB Hard Drive & 128 GB Solid-State Drive, Windows 10 Home (14-cd1042nr, Mineral Silver)

text_fidelity_a:
HP ENVY Photo 7155 All-in-One Photo Printer (K7G93A) and XL Ink Cartridges - 4 Colors This is a multi-functional unit. It scans, prints (papers and photos), and does copies. It has two media trays; one can load 8-1/2x11 paper, and photo paper in the second tray. Prints are of very high quality. I printed beautiful pictures and crisp email messages from my laptop in the living room. You can use the same tray for either 5x7 or 4x6 photo papers. I tried to print separately using my personal computer or work computer, they worked well except that this printer did not work with my chromebook. HP gave a message saying that this printer does not support Chromebook. I could not connect wirelessly to my work laptop, only with USB cables. But my personal computer linked wirelessly. The installation is simple, but took an awful lot of time to download HP programs to get the printer going. This printer also supports mobile printing with iPhone, but I did not try that feature. Another feature that I didn’t have in my previous printer is the use of SD card to print quality pictures. The machine has a SD card port and you can insert the card and print effortlessly. The touch screen interface is easy to operate the printer, but first you need to get familiar with it

Other cons are that it does not have built-in fax capability, and does not have Ethernet network interfaces, which may be an additional feature some users may be looking. Such a feature is an ideal choice for printer sharing with your family or the home office or for business. It is a little heavy and an average size printer. I did not sign up for the "HP Instant Ink" program. You have the choice not to sign up if you don’t want it. But if you are planning on this option, make sure that if you sign up and then cancel your subscription anytime, the printer will not get disabled. I have rated this product three stars for overall satisfaction.

text_fidelity_a:
Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black Update: I have now tried two other brands (a coworker's, and bought another brand) of ergonomic mice that both work substantially better than the Anker version, which also cost less! I highly suggest anyone considering buying this, skip over it and look for another one that is cheaper with good reviews. It amazes me that a company with a known name can skip out on quality so much that other product that cost half as much outperform it in every way.

The Good:
Feels great to hold. More natural than a typical mouse. All the buttons are in the right places and do not require any strain to press. The wheel is in the perfect spot to be used by my middle finger, which is typically what I try to do, since I swear I already have arthritis in my point finger being under 30 years old...

The Bad: There is an obvious input delay, making this pretty terrible for anyone who grew up using computers. That no one else has mentioned this is beyond me. Side by side comparison of any of my Logitech mice and this Anker mouse makes the input delay on this mouse even more obvious. It feels like trying to use a mouse on a TV with interpolation (120 Hz, smooth motion, etc.) enabled. On top of the nearly deal-breaking latency issue, the input into the computer is inconsistent, causing the mouse to frequently skip around or miss my movements.

If you expect to play any game that requires any amount of precision or is time-based, you will regret buying this mouse. Games aside, this mouse reduces my productivity because of how unreliable the signal is, and the extra effort needed to predict the movement of the cursor due to the lag.

I tried the wired version of this mouse (a friend had it) and the input lag is not as bad, but is still there. Therefore, I advise against anyone buying this or the wired version, and suggest to instead look elsewhere.
text_fidelity_b: Anker 2.4G Wireless Vertical Ergonomic Optical Mouse, 800 / 1200 /1600 DPI, 5 Buttons for Laptop, Desktop, PC, Macbook - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White This is the best overview of the components I've seen so far:

Nexia Home Bridge (this is the key component)
Schlage touch screen deadbolt w alarm
Schlage home keypad lock
Schlage home dimmer/appliance module
Schlage home indoor camera
Schlage home outdoor camera
Trane home energy management thermostat
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) remote thermostat
Trane ComfortLink ((tm)) II Control
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) Platinum ZV control (?)
Schlage home door/window sensor
Schlage home motion sensor
Other Z-Wave sensor
Other Z-Wave thermostat
Other Z-Wave lighting device
Other Z-Wave wall switch and outlet

They might have considered making the 9V battery compartment in the "Bridge" just a little bit bigger. It's a mighty snug fit and you have to remove the battery to get the MAC ID. In fact, you have to remove the 9V battery so often it's a curiosity why the battery door is such a pain to remove and why the battery is so difficult to get out of its little bay. I was actually using a flat screwdriver to pry the battery out, it's that tight.

---

Overall, now that the camera, light dimmer and lock and installed, "enrolled" and apparently functional..? WHAT A GREAT SYSTEM!!! The components look great, they're top-quality. Now that I see everything in action (especially video of my home on my iPhone) the subscription fee seems like not such a high price to pay for what you're getting. I know that I'm going to be sorely tempted to add more cameras.

The deadbolt operates with a passcode OR with a physical key. At first I was thinking that you could lock yourself out accidentally but after examining the lock and playing with the buttons I see that is not the case.

I also understand why the light dimmer module goes so well with the indoor camera -- when it gets dark, you'd want to be able to ramp up the light enough for the camera to see! It's a temptation to put the indoor camera in one of my kids room, which is what I might have done when they were small. That would be a rude intrusion these days. So it's outside a hallway that all traffic must pass through. The field of vision nearly covers the two main doors into and out of our home, also. So I can keep an eye on who's getting home when and all that parent-of-teenagers type stuff.

Is there a controller for exterior lights? Or some kind of interface that would allow me to remotely control wired exterior lights?

The only downside to this system, aside from the kludge-y installation process, is that you will want to add more components, and they aren't cheap.

Bottom line: top-quality components, frustrating "enrollment" process -- once you get it all up and running, it's quite impressive. It's nearly worth the frustration to see it all in operation. It would be nice if you could pan-and-zoom the camera. Perhaps that will be forthcoming in another camera model.

I can't help but feel that the process of "enrolling" the components couldn't be made more simple or more streamlined.

Now to budget for an exterior camera... maybe two...

---

Now that I've seen the system in operation I grasp what the manufacturer is actually offering -- remote control of your home administered via your iPhone or iPad. Ideal for working professionals. Getting everything connected and communicating was a little effort, but it's really a beautiful system in operation. You will definitely want to add more light controls and cameras, at least I would. I wonder if there's an exterior light module? There must be. Once you see it in operation the subscription will not be an issue. You are getting more than what you're paying for.

An excellent upgrade to your home and a clever way to keep tabs on a vacation home.
text_fidelity_b: Schlage WCE100 Home Indoor Camera with Nexia Home Intelligence, White

text_fidelity_a:
Zune HD 32 GB Video MP3 Player (Platinum) For the past 5 years or so, I've been rocking it out to a Sandisk Sansa. Those were nice little MP3 players, that in my opinion, were superior to the iPod. Well, the Age of the Touch Screen is here, and I wanted an upgrade. The Zune HD seemed like the only solid choice, if I wanted to avoid loading iTunes onto my computer. So I bought one. So far, I think it's a neat little device that gives me *most* of what I want. The sound quality is great, and I like having the internet in my pocket. Microsoft did a fine job with the OS and software; I've had no problems figuring it out. For web capability, it's a bit small, but then again, I appreciate it's size as an MP3 player. I also really like the touch screen. It's nice and responsive, so no problems there, either. Now here's a list of things I'd like to see:

*Micro SD Card slot
*Google Apps
*Netflix (It supports HD vid, so why not Netflix?!)
*Some sort of email client
*Non-proprietary cable for charging.

So far, Microsoft has done a decent job. I'd give it a B+, and I would also feel good about recommending the device to my friends and family.
text_fidelity_b: Zune HD 32 GB Video MP3 Player (Platinum)

text_fidelity_a: Soundcore by Anker Life P3i Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds, 4 Mics, AI-Enhanced Calls, 10mm Drivers, Powerful Sound, App for Custom EQ, 36H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency, Bluetooth 5.2 These earbuds are currently $60, making them some of the cheapest wireless earbuds that I own. For $60, you get a lot of features including noise cancellation, great battery life, pretty good sound quality, a comfortable secure fit and customizations and updates via the app. Noise cancellation is not fantastic, but many other brands don't any noise cancellation in this price range. 9 hour battery life without recharging is a couple of hours longer than most of my other earbuds. Sound quality is loud and not noisy but sometimes a little muddy in the midrange, but not too bad for this price range. Compared to other earbuds in this price range that I have tried, these are the most comfortable and the most secure fitting. Many other brands don't have any app support for earbuds in this price range, but I love being able to customize the equalization to improve clarity for different types of music. I also love the ability to improve performance and fix bugs with firmware updates, if the company provides them. In summary, I can hear the difference in sound quality and performance difference between these earbuds and $120 earbuds from different brands but I'm not sure the difference is big enough to justify the 2X price difference. If you only have $60 to spend, these are a fine choice for you. If you're the type that is constantly losing wireless earbuds, these aren't so expensive that you will be really upset if you lose them.
text_fidelity_b: Soundcore by Anker Life P3i Hybrid Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds, 4 Mics, AI-Enhanced Calls, 10mm Drivers, Powerful Sound, App for Custom EQ, 36H Playtime, Fast Charging, Transparency, Bluetooth 5.2

Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout) I purchased one of these 9th generation Kindle Oasis. The first unit I received would freeze during the configuration process. You could reset it, but if you try to configure, it would freeze again. At this point, I made the mistake of asking for a replacement instead of just returning the faulty Kindle Oasis for a refund. A replacement unit arrived in three days. Unfortunately, the replacement unit was DoA. There was a fixed image on screen, and I wasn't able to get a response from this Kindle after charging it for a long time and multiple reset attempts. I had already shipped the first unit back using a UPS shipping label created by Amazon at this point. I went to my Amazon Orders page to return the second unit for a credit. But Amazon web interface wouldn't allow a self service return for refund. I had contact customer service and deal with several customer service representatives. They consistently asked me to try some simple trouble shooting steps ( most of which are not even applicable if you have a completely dead kindle). They wouldn't listen to me when I said I just wanted to return it, and try to pressure me into another replacement. At this point, I had spent several hours troubleshooting, talking to Amazon Customer service, taking packages to UPS, etc. so I insisted on a return for refund. This time, the customer service representative said he was having problems generating the return label, and then disappeared. After several minutes of wait, another customer rep took over and worked on this case for another 10 minutes or so. At that point, I ended up with two sets of return labels in my email. The customer service rep told me to use the labels from the second email (in chronological order). So the next day, I shipped the replacement Kindle Oasis back. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the package was delivered to Amazon and three days after this I received an email confirmation from Amazon that my first return was received. A few days later, I saw on UPS tracking that the second Kindle Oasis (replacement) was also received by Amazon. I waited a few days for return confirmation and refund from Amazon, but nothing happened. When I contacted Amazon Customer service, they kept telling me that I shouldn't worry about getting charged as my replacement is complete. But they could see no record of my return of the replacement. I spent probably a good half an hour chatting with a customer service rep but they couldn't help me at all since they could only see the record for on return request. That chat ended with no resolution because I ran out of time and had to get to an appointment. Later, I got in touch with yet another service rep, and explained everything from scratch. Luckily, that person was able to find records of both returns being received by Amazon and finally issued me a refund.

So lessons from this story:
1. Don't buy a 9th gen Kindle Oasis. There seems to be serious quality control issues. The probability of one customer receiving two faulty Kindles in a row would be infinitesimal unless fault rates are in the 20% range.
2. If you receive a faulty Kindle from Amazon, return it for a refund. Don't ask for a replacement. Amazon's automated return process cannot handle the return of a replacement unit, and you will sink a lot of time dealing with customer service representatives
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) – Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 32 GB, Wi-Fi - with Special Offers (Closeout)

text_fidelity_a:
ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange) This tripod is advertised as 65 inches tall, but that is misleading since you can only reach that height with the center post full extended and somewhat unstable. Most tripods are measured with just the legs and not including the center post or head. This one is about 50 inches tall or 57 inches with the included ball head. You can compare that measurement to other brands.

For a tripod of this height, this one is relatively lightweight and folds up into a compact 20-inch-long case. That makes it very portable for field use. However, they did have to make a lot of compromises in stability to make it this compact and lightweight. The legs have 4 sections (compared to 2 or 3 sections on sturdier tripods) and the thinnest sections are somewhat flexy under moderate weight or in a moderate wind. I don't trust this tripod with a mid-weight SLR camera and exposures of more than 1 second (unless you have the legs folded to half length). For a lightweight camera and fast exposure, this tripod is fine. However, I still would not trust extending the center post in windy conditions, since that amplifies the instability of the tripod legs.

The tripod is attractively finished. I do not like all the twist locks that are slow to operate (compared to cam-locks) and with 4 leg sections, this tripod has lots of twist-locks.

The ball head works OK for this price level and has a quick release plate that also works OK. This company has several different quick release plates sold separately, hopefully one of those will work with this tripod so you can easily use different cameras on it. I have not tried to figure out which one to buy yet, though.

Other people are complaining about the zipper on the case. The zipper on my case broke on the first day of use, too. Just the zipper pull, which is not too expensive to replace.

In summary, this tripod works OK for this price level if you are using a smaller camera and fast exposures. If their goal was to make a lightweight portable tripod, I wish they had made it sturdier and shorter instead of flimsy and taller.
text_fidelity_b: ZOMEi Tripod, 65" Camera Tripod for Canon Nikon DSLR, Aluminum Alloy Tripod with 360 Degree Ball Head, Professional Tripod for Travel and Work (Orange)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire Kids Edition Tablet, 7" Display, 8 GB, Blue Kid-Proof Case (Previous Generation - 5th) Very disappointed in Amazon. They ALMOST Got it right. Returned this one quickly.

Let me be clear I am an Amazon Fangirl. I have consistently tried their new things, I have subscribed to prime for years, I love amazon. I love their kindles. So I don't often speak ill of my precious amazon.

I wanted to upgrade my son's kindle ( First gen Fire HD7 ) it's charging port is a bit wobbly and damaged, we've used it for many years and it's got a little wear. That said, it works BETTER Than the current kindle fire. The only problem is you can't play all the same games that I can play on my other kindle and you can't on the new one either. It wants the "NEW HD" ( or my HDX) to play certain games.

Where to begin....first of all the new OS Sucks. It just does. so bad. I'm not even going to rant on that because it's user preference but I found the old OS to be more user friendly and responsive. I have an HDX and it's by far the top notch of them all. I hope I don't have to "upgrade" to this OS.

Storage & Offline use:
You only have 8gb of storage, which wouldn't be an issue thanks to the upgradable microsd slot.. ( GOOD CALL AMAZON) ..EXCEPT They crippled the functionality. For example, I go to the grocery store or road tip with my kid and I let him watch or play on his kindle without being on wifi, you can't do that anymore. Your kids can NOT Watch movies that are downloaded to the microsd card when you are offline. You can't. Not allowed. You can't operate much of anything in the kids profile if you are not connected to wifi. Having 128bg SD card is USELESS for your kids when offline.
I've bought loads of disney movies and the digital copies are all on Amazon for the very reason that they were great to download to our other kindles and watch when we were in the car, plane, or costco.

It won't even let you START The kids freetime profile if you are offline. This severely cripples the device for no good reason. Games and movies which are downloaded to the device or the SD card should work offline in most cases. I've done it on my HDX and my first gen hd. Works just fine in freetime on older devices. No reason for this. And before someone tells me that's what you expect when you stream...I'm not talking about streaming or using netflix, I'm talking about content downloaded to the device. Irrationally Amazon decided that if you are not online, you can go kick rocks.
If you are in an ADULT Profile, I think you can, although I did not try to be fair, because I bought the KIDS Edition for a reason, for my kid to use it.I have my own kindle. No sense in having this for kids if you can't use it when you're out and about. Everyone knows that the screen is the ultimate "quiet time" reward in our parent tool-kit. If you say it's not you're either a liar or an over taxed helicopter parent with way too much techno anxiety. Joking...sorry not sorry.

Kindle FreeTime "unlimited"....
I use the freetime for my son ALL THE TIME. It's amazing, it limits him to what *I* want him to play and watch. I can set a timer for weekends/weekdays that go off at bedtime so that he can "read", watch a show, or play for a short time as a reward before bed. The freetime is
the number one reason I have not gone with an iPad or other device. I can't give my kid any other device with the same level of comfort and control of his screen time and content. I HIGHLY recommend kindles to all my parent friends for this exact reason. It's WELL Worth it. However...it's NOT worth it to use "Unlimited" on this new device. The new kindle sucks for freetime ( See above reason on offline freetime) Mainly tho...it's TERRIBLE for the parent if you've mistakenly turned ON Kindle unlimited. ( If you have an older child, say 9yrs+ this can be mitigated with a nice sit down convo) I'll explain...

Why Freetime Unlimited SUCKS:
I'm speaking of the paid Unlimited service here, the main feature of freetime is still great, with some exceptions ( above) on the new device.

Every single app they touch it will download. If they are curious, and want to see what the game is they instinctively click the app, completely unaware that they have 8gb of space on their tablet and actually it's more like 4gb after the OS. This makes it run Slooooooow and crash. Crash a lot. Crash within the first 60 minutes of your child using the device. Until you go in and fix it, meaning delete them all individually, this device is annoyingly slow and unresponsive. I found out, you can get the apps to download or move them to the memory card, but it will still slow you down once that fills up and you still have to do regular maintaince on the devices memory. The first year of this is free, with this device, but I promise you it's more annoying than worth it. I was an early unlimited subscriber at $2.99 a month and I cancelled it rather quickly, even on my far better HDX and the first gen kindle it was STILL Annoying.

If you have an OLDER Child...this may be mitigated with a sit down conversation as to how their device works, what downloading means, and their storage space. My child is 5, and has proven to not exactly get the concept and download everything willy nilly if given the option.

Do yourself a favor....buy the HD Version, Pray they didn't cripple offline freetime on it, buy the extra warranty and case and and try that instead. That's what I plan to do, I'm going to give it a wait and see if they improve the HD device on the next round. Since the first gen HD 7 still works better than this one, I'll hold out.

Please Amazon....try to get it right next time.
Thanks,
Just another mom.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Kids Edition Tablet, 7" Display, 8 GB, Blue Kid-Proof Case (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a:
Ring Alarm 5 Piece Kit (1st Gen) – Home Security System with optional 24/7 Professional Monitoring – No long-term contracts – Works with Alexa The most popular review on here, Kyle’s from Oct 2018, has a lot of good points such as praising the system where it works right and suggestions for how it could be improved such as the need for a duress code.

The only major thing that review missed is the range extenders.
They are almost worthless.

If you read the reviews of the range extender when sold as a separate item you will read about some of the issues.

Issue 1: They are weak. People’s reviews and reviews from electronics publications find these extenders to be underpowered. There are many more powerful z wave range extenders in the market.

When I called tech support about this they blatantly told me they knew about the poorly performing range extenders.

They told me that some of the Ring compatible smart outlets made by other manufacturers, like GE, include range extended and that they work much better than the Ring range extenders.

At least the tech support person was honest in admitting that their extenders sucked and that compatible third party manufacturer extenders will work better...I guess?

There is a page on the Ring website that list all the Z wave devices made by third parties that are compatible with the Ring system.

Unfortunately you can’t buy the best reviewed and most powerful Z wave range extenders on the market because Ring does not make them compatible with their system because they want you to buy their crappy extenders of course.

I guess we should just be grateful that at least some of the compatible smart plugs have signal extenders built into them that are better than Ring’s.

Issue 2: They are dumb. The algorithms for determining what path a device takes, in terms of whether it connects to a certain range extender or the base station, is horrible. This flaw includes the range extenders themselves when they try and decide whether or not to connect to the base station or another range extender. (I have two Ring range extenders).

If you have one range extender 20-30 feet from the base station and then place another range extender 20-30 feet from the first range extender branching out in the same direction there is no guarantee that the second range extender will connect to the first range extender rather than trying to connect to the base station.

Maybe this is because the signal from the range extenders is so bad that the devices are programmed to connect to the base station if at all possible, even if the signal is weak.

One support tech even told me a “funny” story about how a friend of theirs has a range extender just fifteen feet away from the base station in their house and but the range extended chooses to connect to another range extender that is more than 40 feet away rather than directly to the base station that is just 15 feet from it.

Ha ha ha, it’s SO funny when your expensive electronic product that you bought to keep your home safe does not work correctly! Hilarious!

A secondary criticism is that if the signal to the keypad isn’t strong enough the keypad alarm might not sound.

I have two doors between my keypad and the range extender it connects to.
When the doors are open the keypad usually sounds the alarm, when they are closed it never does.

It would seem obvious to any rational person that the issue with the alarm not sounding is the signal strength but the tech support people swear up and down that that is not possible.

Even when the doors are closed the tech support people claim the keypad reads as having an adequate signals strength ( the tech support people can see the signal strength of your devices but you can’t).

They are actually sending me a new keypad but I am not hopeful it will solve the problem.
It seems obvious to me that the command for signaling the alarm requires a better signal than the other functions of the keypad.

Maybe the signal for the alarm is only sent out once while the signal for the other functions are repeatedly sent out until the base station acknowledges them? Who knows?

The point is that it seems like a design flaw and if you plan on having your keypad more than a room lengths away from your base station you shouldn't count on the alarm on the keypad working.

I will update this review with the performance of my replacement keypad.

The last thing I will say is that the price of 11 dollars a month for monitoring the entire system regardless of how many devices you have, including any cameras, is a great price.

I hope that this type of price is here to stay. If they pull a bait and switch where they significantly increase the price of monitoring after they initially get enough people to buy the system I will drop this system like a hot potato and sell it used on eBay.
text_fidelity_b: Ring Alarm 5 Piece Kit (1st Gen) – Home Security System with optional 24/7 Professional Monitoring – No long-term contracts – Works with Alexa

Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black) Taken for what this is supposed to be, this is a fabulous machine. It's not a primary computer. It's not a laptop replacement. If you need a low power/ultra-portable computer, go with a netbook.

This is more of a mutt. It's a portable media player that doesn't have as much storage as an iPod or a Zen, but has a larger, higher quality screen and a kickstand, which makes it easier to watch movies at a desk.

It can read ebooks. It's not quite as light or comfortable for long term reading as a Kindle, but it can support full color images. It's far superior for this purpose than any of the other devices Amazon has put out an app for.

It can run Windows 7. It's not a full powered machine, but it's even smaller than a netbook.

It fits a slot somewhere between a PDA/smartphone and a netbook, and it's brilliant.

I would have liked a larger hard drive, an SD card (it would have gotten 5 stars if it had one) and more than one USB slot. There is no ethernet port. It only connects wirelessly. The optional port replicator gives you Ethernet and two more USB slots, but still no SD.

A few things to keep in mind. When you're first setting it up, you can't access the virtual keyboard button, so you need to use the Ease of Access icon to get to that. Windows will say to press the space bar to activate the feature. Use the mouse click button (marked +).

The design is very sleek. It's comfortable to hold and work with. The screen has an adjustable brightness, which is easier on the eyes, and easier to use in bright sunlight. The low glare screen helps with this as well.

Overall, this is bleeding edge, early adopter technology.
text_fidelity_b: Archos 9 PC Windows 7 Starter Tablet (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro) I began researching these based on reviewing another popular brand. I am a stickler for detail and after hours of research and asking questions I decided to give these a try because of the cost and positive reviews. I bought these for my elderly parent (90 years old) who has hearing loss but does not wear a hearing aid.
After a couple weeks of use I can honestly say these things are great! Very easy to install, easy to use for an elderly person not technically savvy, works from a long distance (we tried the next room), and the volume of these units can go very loud which is good for all types of hearing. There is also a balance control in case a person hears differently in both ears, and a switch to change from normal to higher or lower frequencies to help those with that type of hearing loss.
We can now watch TV when visiting my parent without the TV being so loud. But it is hard to verbally communicate with each other when they wear the headphones, but that’s not a big deal.
You can turn down the TV as low as needed, even muted, but the headphones can be as loud as needed. We used the RCA output from their TV (a 4 year old flat screen) and that works great. We tried it on a new flat screen and worked well also (digital output). All cables are provided along with extra ear inserts.
I like the fact this uses 2.4GHz instead of Bluetooth or infrared which often can lose connection with interference or movement away from the base station. I went out of the room into the next room and heard this one just fine.
The weight was a concern for me but my parent only watches TV for no more than 2 hours at the time and they said it was fine. There are ear loops provided to help with holding the unit if needed.
The only issue I found was that the input on the base station to charge the headphones was oriented backwards to how a person takes off the headset (have to turn the headset around to charge). And when putting on from the base station you have to turn the headphones around else you’ll put it on backwards which is not a big deal, but the volume button and balance will be reversed meaning my parent the first time turned the balance thinking it was volume and thought something was wrong. That’s one more thing for an elderly person to remember, plus you don’t need a lot of pressure to bend/break the charging prongs in the base unit if installed the wrong way.
We used the “speaker” option one time and it worked pretty well to allow a person to hear conversations in the room.

I’ll update this review should something change, but for now I highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: SIMOLIO 2.4G Analog Wireless TV Headsets with 100ft Transmit Range, No Pairing, No Delay, TV Voice Highlighting Headphones for Seniors, Wireless TV Headphones with Extra Soft Earbuds (SM-823 Pro)

text_fidelity_a:
Zmodo Pivot 1080p 360° Rotating Wireless Security Camera and All-in-One Smart Home Hub No Sensor Included Unboxing: Two circles of tape, one at each end of a printed box sheath. Good quality plain blue box underneath with Zmodo logo. The presentation is nice enough to make it a good gift, without veering into making you pay for packaging. Within are cord, window/door sensors, and device, all well protected for shipping. Device is black, but cords and window sensors are all white. Protective film of plastic over the lens.

The device itself is about the diameter of a coffee cup, but with an aspect more like a drink can. It's a mix of matte black and a shiny black that attracts lint like a magnet.
Three rubber feet raise it above the table. A speaker is inset underneath. Made in China. Model number is on the bottom. It feels like a good quality device. There is a chemical smell, but I think it's coming from the instructions, not the camera. The power socket is ungrounded wall outlet to MicroUSB, which is a bit tired, but at least very common and compatible. I wish Europe would reduce their regulations enough to assist the adoption of USB C.

Plugged it in. The ring on top lights up green and blinks. Then the camera pans around once and has a look around.

Downloaded and installed the Zmodo app, which has really polarized reviews and needs access to:
Device and App history
Identity
Contacts
Location
SMS
Phone
Photos/Media/Files
Camera
Microphone
Wifi connection
Device ID and Call information
I can see why the needs permissions for most of that, but it is still a lot of access if anyone were in a position to abuse it.

Opened the app, gave it an email address and password to create an account.

Clicked Add Device, then Wireless Device.

Clicked the check mark twice, and then entered WiFi password.

Waited while things blinked for about a minute. Ring changed from green flashy, to blue flashy, to blue solid. Camera has another look around and does some clicking.

Named the device and gave it a password.

Clicked on the still image that looked like it came from the camera and was into the live feed, displayed on my Android smart phone (Galaxy S6). Clicking on the arrows on either side of the screen turns the camera. apparently, it can see in any direction, but once it gets to a certain point, it needs to turn around and go the other way, it can't just keep spinning.

Thus far, everything seems to be working except the motion tracking, which was kind of the main selling point. I have it turned on in phone settings. Looking at their support pages, it seems that it won't motion track once you gave been in the room a while. They recommended I leave the room for 10 minutes and come back so that the microwave array will find me interesting again. Also, apparently you can view your feed on a computer by logging in on their website.

After leaving for ten minutes and then returning to the room and sitting near it, it took about a minute for it to notice something was amiss, at which point it did a slow scan of the whole room and snapped a picture of me when it saw me move. It then stopped, still looking in the wrong direction.

My end verdict is that it's actually quite a bit nicer than previous wifi cameras I've tested, but falls far short of what I would like to see in a motion tracking camera. The motion tracking is slow and dense, when it works at all. There are enough additional features, like using as a speaker, communicating with someone through it, temperature and humidity data, etc, to give it a more versatile set of uses, but without the motion detection/control being solid, it all feels thrown together and tacked on.

I received a sample for review but opinions are my own.
text_fidelity_b: Zmodo Pivot 1080p 360° Rotating Wireless Security Camera and All-in-One Smart Home Hub No Sensor Included

What is TERRIBLE: Security camera features. Bottom of the barrel. There is a sensitivity to motion slider for when the camera starts, but that is ALL. No way of mapping out areas you want to ignore (e.g sidewalk or pets). "Free" cloud is a rippoff. You get 8 SECOND highly compressed clips!! That's it. If you store locally on an SD card you can get up to 30 seconds.

If you want this camera for security monitoring, unless 8 second snippets work for you, look elsewhere. You can't even pay them to get longer recordings. Since I bought this thing because of the free cloud service, I consider this a total ripoff. Dishonest.

Through the windows app: The settings are confusing. The interface is awful. You can't set it to automatically open a live view. Instead you have to open & click on an icon. You can't leave it in live view (it will automatically shut off after a little while "to save battery." Isn't that my choice? I should be able to use the battery if I want to. I like to leave the live view open when I'm expecting someone.

I would not buy this again. Look to the real brands like linksys, Nest, Ring, etc. if you actually want a security camera and not a little toy.

Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229 This will be a fairly detailed and honest review.

1. Who is this for?
This computer is what I would consider a gateway computer. Those who are looking at upgrading a fairly old or not so powerful laptop and are looking to do a little more productivity, this is a great option.

2. What do you get?
Well you can probably read the description, however it's worth noting. You get an Intel i7 7500u CPU (dual core with 4 threads) 12gb DDR4 RAM, Nvidia 940mx GPU, a 256gb SSD, 15.6" 1080p screen, fingerprint reader, and a backlit keyboard.

The reason I mention all of the feautures is because you would be hardpressed to find another laptop with these features for the same price. To my knowledge there is not laptop on the market for $800 with an i7, dedicated graphics, 12gb of RAM and an SSD. This is really one of the best values on the market right now.

With all of that said, this isn't for everyone. If you want to do extensive gaming, this is not for you. Can it game? Yes, light gaming can be achieved, however it isn't marketed as a gaming laptop. Is this for someone who wants to do editing (video, audio, photos)? Yes, again light editing can be achieved.

What blew me away with this computer is the speakers! They are fantastic! I usually use headphones and would consider myself somewhat picky with sound, and for laptop speakers these are really something great.

This computer is really a middle of the pack all arounders dream. If you dabble in a little of this and a little of that but don't do anything professionally or extremely serious, this is really all you need.

Also, everyone's experience is different. Some hate loud fans, and if this is pushed the fans will be audible. Some don't like that the backlit keyboard times out after 30 seconds of no use. These things really don't bother me.

Lastly, the versatility of this laptop is really great. I've bought tablets and sold them because I couldn't justify having a laptop and tablet, then bought tablets again because I missed the things I could do with them that I was missing on a laptop. This solved all of those issues except size. It's pretty big, which for some is a plus others its not.

Overall, if you are looking at upgrading and don't want to spend $1,200-2,000 on a flagship model laptop this is a great option! I can't recommend this enough.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire R 15 2-in-1 Laptop, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 7th Gen Intel Core i7, GeForce 940MX, 12GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, R5-571TG-7229

It is USB 3.0 compatible, and worked fine on a USB 3.0 port on a Win 7 machine. It also worked just as well (albeit slower) on a USB 2.0 port on a Win 7 and an XP machine. Simple plug and play, with no drivers needed. It comes with a USB cable.

The reader is compact, measuring just under 3.5 inches long and about 1.75 inches wide. It's very low profile, standing about ½ inch tall. The card slots are on the front, and the USB connection is on the back.

Simple, straightforward and works well. That's pretty much all I need in a card reader. Hopefully it will last longer than my previous one - I'll update the review should this not perform well over time.

1080P HD Projector, 5G WiFi Movie Projector, UUO Home Theater Support 4K Video Projector, Synchronize Smartphone Screen, Dolby Audio Support-Compatible with TV Stick/iOS/Android/Smartphone/PS5 This is a decent entry level projector for every day use and a very good unit for specialized purposes like outdoor viewing on a large screen.

Its picture quality is better than most I have seen in this range and is brighter as well. The native 1080p image is sufficient for what you are buying, but one would never compare it to a higher end model. Of course, most of those start by adding another zero to the price, just for starters. I have had a couple of projectors in this price range and none of them really have a "great" picture, and that's honestly to be expected.

With this projector, you get a watchable image in daylight hours, but really improves if you black-out the room with darkening curtains or are watching after dark. The image will clearly show on a light color wall, but will improve drastically if you use an actual screen.

The fan noise is a little more intrusive than I would like, so it does interfere a bit if you are just using the included speakers. My suggestion is to connect it to a stand-alone external speaker setup. This is especially recommended if you are setting up an outdoor viewing screen.

It does tout 4D±50° Keystone correction, but it's not really as good as all that, in my opinion. I could never get the picture shape quite right at these angles. Connectivity is adequate, with several input options, so that's really a plus. I had it hooked up to an external hard drive as well as my Amazon Fire Stick and it handled each of them nicely. The WiFi connection is adequate and I had no issues connecting to my network. 5G connection is definitely a plus here as long as you are relatively close to your router.

Overall, I would say that this projector is a good value for the money spent. Try it out to see if Projection Television is for you. It's a whole new world, that's for sure. I don't miss going to the cinema as much anymore. Watching movies on the "Big Screen" at home is so convenient... and the popcorn is much cheaper.
text_fidelity_b: 1080P HD Projector, 5G WiFi Movie Projector, UUO Home Theater Support 4K Video Projector, Synchronize Smartphone Screen, Dolby Audio Support-Compatible with TV Stick/iOS/Android/Smartphone/PS5

text_fidelity_a:
Shure SRH145m+ Portable Collapsible Headphones with Remote + Microphone Compatible with All Apple iOS Devices Update after 4 months

They have got more comfortable. I don't use them often so I don't think it's my ears that have got used to them I think the material has gotten softer with use and maybe the band has stretched out a bit.

I'll add to my review that while these are not hard to drive they are not easy to drive either. They are near the top of easy to drive. They are 32 ohms and sensitivity is 96db. What does that mean? I use these mostly with my computer that has a pretty good sound chip and I find that I have to have the computer sound (windows 7) and the music app (foobar 2000) volume all the way up to get these to where they open up and sound best. In general, they need to be a little louder than I would like to sound their best.

Sound wise I find myself punching up the bass a bit. They need a little bit more hit and a touch of bloom for things like the bass guitar and kik drum to sound about right. Not a lot, just a 3db boost from about 80 to 200hz. I also find they need a bit of a push at 10K and up to put a little more air around the instruments. With more listening, I'm not quite as thrilled with the sound as I was, but I still like them. Hours of listing do not leave me with ear fatigue and they do not punish poorly recorded music.

Update after a month:
These have not got more comfortable and I kinda wish I had returned them but for $32 it's not really worth it given I'd get charged $5 for the return. These hurt after a couple of hours and no amount of moving them around relieves it. The material is soft enough but I think it is too soft and packs down. Also clamping pressure is pretty high on my melon so now that I'm keeping them I may try to stretch them out a bit

================================================================

I am FUSSY about sound! I want natural neutral sound. That's what you get with these. The bass is natural, drums sound pretty good. Sibilance is there but not annoying. They are accurate without being clinical or fatiguing. They are musical without being over warm or polite. They do not punish poorly recorded music like some more HiFi headphones do. There is a nice amount of 'air' around the instruments but not much of a sound stage beyond that. They are a nice middle of the road set of headphone, not too bright, but bright enough, a good mid-range, pretty well-controlled bass without much bleed and some bass extension. They could use a touch more bloom to suit my tastes but what is there suits me fine. If I thought they were bass shy I would tell you.

I use a 15 band equalizer on my computer and I end up putting some EQ on most headphones I use, but I found with these I liked them best with no EQ. They do not go super loud with my phone. Loud enough for me, but not might be loud enough if you like your music really loud.They need a little volume to sound there best but that's pretty typical and I have had headphones that needed to be louder to sound their best.

They have one big problem. They are not very comfortable. I would not get these if wearing them all day at work is your thing of if comfort is really important to you because you get annoyed if they are not comfortable. In comparison, the Sennheiser HD 2.20 is WAY more comfortable. The foam is too thin and you almost feel like the plastic is pressed against your ears. They 2nd day they felt a little better. My ears getting used to them, or maybe the foam adapting to the shape of my ears or a little bit of both.The headband cushion is also really thin but did not bother me as much as the earpieces.

They have almost no isolation. My old open back Sennheiser 239 had more isolation. I'm also not a fan of how round that headband is but I guess they did that so they would fold up smaller? I don't know but I wish the fit a little closer to the head on the sides.

The cable is kind of weird in that the right and left cords are side by side like lamp cord and a little thicker than on other budget headphones.

Between my old Senn 239, and the Senn 2.20 and the Jabra Move (I think it was the Move) I like the sound of these Shure the best by far. If these cost $50 or even $60 I'd be really happy with these, at least for sound. For $30 dollars I'm REALLY happy with them.

I'd be tempted to knock a star off for comfort but for me, the sound is everything so the 5 stars are for the sound.
text_fidelity_b: Shure SRH145m+ Portable Collapsible Headphones with Remote + Microphone Compatible with All Apple iOS Devices

IPOW 360 Degree Rotatable Break-Resistant iPad Tripod Mount Adapter, Universal Tablet Clamp Holder Fits Ipad, Ipad Air, Pro, Mini, Microsoft Surface, Nexus, for Tripod Monopod, Selfie Stick,Tabletop What a great idea! When I saw this CD slot mounting thing, I was thrilled to be given one in return for an honest review. We have resisted getting a smart phone for long time because of the price but recently signed up for an account with Spring and got a Samsung Galaxy 6 as part of the deal. But the idea of doing some kind of cumbersome mount in the car was not appealing, especially after our experience with a GPS unit several years ago that we never used because all the mounts we tried were awful and more trouble than they were worth.

This mounted perfectly, and securely, in the CD slot (which we very rarely use), but it would also mount in a vent slot if wide enough. You can adjust the direction and angle of your device until you get it how it works best for you, then tighten everything down to lock it in.

The printed instructions are good, but the one thing they don't tell you is not to be timid about it. The piece that holds the device (with the notches) snaps onto what they refer to as "the outstanding round stick," which is the knob/ball bearing part of the holder. At first I thought it was not going to fit, but then I realized I needed to push on it fairly firmly to get it to snap to the ball. After that, you can move the device holder around at varying angles to get it like you want it, then tighten down the big round screw that fits between the two pieces to lock the position.

I also wasn't totally clear on how the CD/vent slot part was supposed to mount, thinking it would shove up inside the CD player like a CD would. It doesn't. It fits in a little ways, not far, and then you turn the triangular-headed screw to raise up the plate until it is wide enough to hold it firmly. It works well, and it doesn't damage your CD player at all. The device holder also takes forceful pulling to widen it to accommodate your device, so you should put your device into it before putting the whole thing into the CD or vent slot. It will snap back snugly against the device, so be careful not to release it too quickly. Once the mount is installed in the slot, if you need to adjust the angle, you can by loosening the round screw slightly and making the adjustment. Our CD slot is up at the top of the dashboard, so the phone is positioned up closer to eye level so we can look at the phone while driving more easily. If your CD slot is down low, you might want to use a vent slot instead.

What I really love about this product is how neat and tidy it is. It solves a problem, and it does it inexpensively and without looking shoddy. A very nice, creative product for cellphone or small GPS users.
text_fidelity_b: IPOW 360 Degree Rotatable Break-Resistant iPad Tripod Mount Adapter, Universal Tablet Clamp Holder Fits Ipad, Ipad Air, Pro, Mini, Microsoft Surface, Nexus, for Tripod Monopod, Selfie Stick,Tabletop
