text_fidelity_a:
Logitech MX Keys Mini Minimalist Wireless Illuminated Keyboard, Compact, Bluetooth, Backlit, USB-C, Compatible with Apple macOS, iOS, Windows, Linux, Android, Metal Build - Graphite I’ve been using the Logitech MX Keys Mini for about two weeks now. I like it, but I don’t love it. The keyboard won’t replace my current favored mechanical keyboard, I love linear switches too much, but it has some uses.

The typing experience is decent. The keyboard is at a fixed angle, it cannot be adjusted. The bottom of the keyboard does have rubber “feet” so that it doesn’t slide around. No movement on my desk mat or plain desktop. The keys have what Logitech calls a “spherical dish” which looks like a little cup on the top of each key. My fingers naturally settle in the indentation but it’s not something I notice when typing.

The keyboard isn’t silent, but it’s much, much quieter than a mechanical keyboard. There’s a little tactile feedback, so I do feel the keypresses, which I like.

The form factor of the keyboard is, well, mini. The size makes it a good solution if you don’t have a lot of space on your desk or want to take it on the go. Logitech made some sacrifices with keys, but did keep the arrow keys. Whew. If you need a numpad, this isn’t the keyboard for you.

I really wish the backlighting could be controlled via the keyboard. The brightness can be adjusted, but that’s it. Otherwise, the keyboard is “smart” enough to know when you are typing and illuminate, but when your hands aren’t on it, or you stop typing for a few seconds, the backlighting turns off. When I’m using my computer in the dark, reading an article or watching something, it’s really annoying to have the backlighting flicker in and out.

The backlighting and other customization options are set in Logi Options, Logitech’s software. I already use Logi Options for my MX Master 3 mouse, but try as I might, I could not get the software to recognize the keyboard. I have to use High Sierra for a program I rely on, and after going through a bunch of suggested troubleshooting, I think that’s why. So if you’re like me and using an older version of macOS, you might have trouble getting the keyboard recognized by Logi Options. Because of this, I can’t use Flow, either.

The MX Keys Mini can connect with up to 3 devices at once, the first three function keys allow quick switching between devices. I tried to pair my MacBookPro and Note20 Ultra to test this, and was able to easily pair both and switch. The keyboard ONLY connects to devices via Bluetooth or the Logi Bolt USB Receiver (which isn’t included). A USB-A to USB-C cable is included for charging only. Because I can’t get Logi Options to recognize the keyboard, I can’t check battery life and know when it needs to be charged.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech MX Keys Mini Minimalist Wireless Illuminated Keyboard, Compact, Bluetooth, Backlit, USB-C, Compatible with Apple macOS, iOS, Windows, Linux, Android, Metal Build - Graphite

GE Personal Security Keychain Alarm, Extra Loud 120 Decibel Siren, Pull Pin Activated, Built In LED Light, Personal & Portable Safety, Emergency, Self Defense, Easy to Use, 51208 I bought several of these for our home and my mother's home. Super loud, and will stop or at least make it difficult for a door to be opened wide enough for an intruder to enter. I tested one out on my husband by placing it at the door he normally enters through. It stopped him, scared him and did just what I hoped it would do. He kind of got mad at me and hollered a few explicatives but it was worth it! We have one door that is on a raised threshold so I set the door stop alarm on a book and the door hits it squarely when opened just a little bitty bit. It's loud - ear piercing loud and that's good as it should scare the bejeebers out of a bad person. On doors that have windows through which the unwanted guest might peer through and see the doorstop, just by placing a light weight towel or papers over it disguises completely. They'll just think your a slob and leave newspapers on the floor.

My mom was thrilled with her doorstops. Anything to help parents stay safe is money well-spent.

Be aware of how all of your doors open since they won't do any good on doors that open to the outside. The 9 volt battery was a tad difficult to install but I'm not complaining. For my mom I had to write in big letters with a felt permanent marker ON and OFF so she could easily turn them off when not in use and not waste batteries or scare her by an accidental alarm. We'll be taking some of these with us on vacation. These are really great!

UPDATE: December 1, 2011 - I have bought several more of these because they are so practical and good at what they do. I've learned to pick them up by holding the sides of them lest I accidentally hit the metal plate on top and hear it's ear-breaking scream. I've taken at least one of these on overnight trips to put against the door in our hotel rooms. It makes me feel a lot safer knowing this thing will scream if someone tries to break in.

text_fidelity_a:
Actiontec 300 Mbps Wireless-N ADSL Modem Router (GT784WN) DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT. I am a Centurylink/Qwest customer of over 25 years. I have a old Actiontec Q1000 router/modem. My DSL Ethernet connection to my desk top has gone down for hours at a time lately. My wifi goes out 10-12 times daily as of late. Small one story house with only two old, non gamer people with latest model $800 smart phones. I read the online instructions and even watched Actiontec video for installing this product. I had a problem and called 1-888-436-0657 the tech support number listed in the Quick Start Guide. Actiontec's phone answering tree makes it very clear that they will not provide any tech support for products purchased from Amazon or any other "unauthorized dealers". I pressed 0 and they hung up on me three seperate times. The Amazon listing for this product made it very clear that it would work with Centturylink. It has a big check mark for Centurylink.

I have spent so many hours on the phone, through email and chat mode with Centurylink it is embarrassing. I offered to pay Centurylink to have a tech come to my home and install my new router/modem. Centurylink said their techs were not allowed to install router/modems but would check my outside wiring for free and my inside wiring for $85 minimun. Centurylink told me they would be happy to have a tech walk me through my hookup via telephone. After I finally was connected to a Centurylink tech and was verified they advised me they were not "allowed" to offer tech support to their customers on this product. They made it sound like it was a federal felony to offer tech support on this product.

Best Buy in New Mexico, and apparently all other retailers no longer carry any products compatible with Centurylink DSL because of their refusal to offer tech support. I heard that Amazon is having so many issues with router/modems that they are reluctant to take returns. I guess I will be taking the $67 loss. I should have rememberd my latin "caveat emptor".

Canon 2562A002 EF 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 is USM Standard Zoom Lens for Canon SLR Cameras The Canon 28-135mm f/3.5-5.6 lens with Image Stabilization is a very capable, and more importantly, affordable lens,and is perfect for times when you just want to have one lens on the camera but you also want to have a lot of options with your focal range. While you get the benefits of a slight wide to telephoto range in one handy package, you do lose in light stops as you move through the focal range (the maximum aperture stops down as you move toward the telephoto end of the range). This is where the image stabilization comes in very handy, and allows you to keep hand shake at bay even when you have to compromise on shutter speed to get the correct exposure.

I've had no complaints about the optical quality, I think you'll be pleased with the shots you get from it - the lens may be cheap but don't confuse that with what the quality of image this lens can provide. Keep in mind on a camera with a cropped sensor (any Canon DSLR model other than the 5D and 1D models) the focal range is equivalent to @45-215mm - you lose a bit of the wide angle advantage, but you get more telephoto, so it depends which end of the focal range you value the most as to whether that is a disadvantage or not.

text_fidelity_a:
Bose CineMate 1 SR Home Theater Speaker System (Black) The Bose CineMate 1SR digital home theater speaker system arrived in perfect condition. It was very well packed inside the Bose box with styrofoam and plastic sheeting, then that box was packed inside another box. The Bose box appeared totally undamaged as if I drove it home from the store myself. After unpacking I was surprised at how light the components were. The speaker array was about the same weight as the Acoustimass module. I am female and could easily pick up and carry them. Everything you need is included in the kit. The cables included are: optical digital, coaxial digital, stereo audio and the power cord. Also included are: remote control, ADAPTiQ audio calibration headset, two AA batteries, Acoustimass module feet, Speaker array extension feet, DVD set-up demonstration, Set-up guide manual, Operating guide manual and Universal Remote Device Codes booklet. We did not have to purchase or hunt down anything to complete the set-up. I recommend watching the DVD set-up movie that is included with the system. It discusses several levels that are important to follow when setting up your system. It also includes various music genres to let you hear the acoustics of your new Bose system.

Set up was relatively easy. My husband and I followed the directions carefully using the included guide for the set-up process and had it up and running in about 30 minutes. We connected the Bose speaker system to our 37" Sharp Aquos HDTV purchased in 2007 and can be found here: http://www.amazon.com/Sharp-Aquos-LC37D43U-37-Inch-720p/dp/B000MKWDJE/ref=cm_cr-mr-title. We also connected it to our Toshiba HDDVD player which can be found here: http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000U62N1S/ref=wms_ohs_product. And we also connected our Roku streaming player (http://www.amazon.com/Roku-2-HD-Streaming-Player/dp/B005DOUJL8/ref=cm_cr-mr-title) by using the included coaxial cables. Just connect one end to the A/V out port on the back of the Roku and the other inputs into the TV input on the back of the speaker array. So, altogether, we have the Bose system connected to our TV, DVD player and the Roku streaming player.

I used the calibration headset and did as instructed in order to calibrate the speaker system to the dimensions of our room and the 5 most used sitting spots. I found it interesting to listen to the various tones the system emitted. I have read some of the other reviews where some people were unhappy that the Bose system did not include an on-screen menu in order to make adjustments to the audio output. My opinion concerning that is this is the purpose of the audio calibration procedure. It is supposed to make the adjustments for you by reflecting sound off the various substrates in your room depending upon where you are positioned at the time. So, I have no problem not having access to an on-screen menu for that.

In our situation, we have our TV, DVD player and Roku sitting in our entertainment cabinet which sits catty-cornered in the far corner of our living room. The soundbar fits perfectly below the TV and does not interfere with the IR signal coming from the TV remote. The speaker array is black and matches perfectly the black of our Sharp television set. The corner where our loveseat and sofa meet is approximately 13 feet almost directly in front of the speaker array. The module sits on the floor (carpeted) beside the TV cabinet.

So now, what do we (husband and I) think about this system?

It is now replacing our Sony SS-MCT100 soundbar system and there really is no comparison as the Bose blows the Sony out of the water. When we got the Sony we thought it sounded pretty good, but now I can clearly hear the difference between the two. The Sony would not get loud enough on some movies even at full volume we had to turn on the stereo speakers to get the sound loud enough and then it would be somewhat distorted. When we first powered up the Bose it was instant volume. I wanted to see just how loud it would get but my husband yelled at me to turn it down. I still have yet to hear just how loud this system will get. We listened to the various music genre provided on the included DVD and I cranked it up until it was almost at cover your ears level. I listened acutely for any distortions, vibrations or any sounds that were the result of something going wrong. I detected nothing other than pure, loud, clear beautiful sound. It was a nice experience. Also, others reported having difficulty in hearing human speech in certain situations. I didn't have any problems hearing what was being said no matter how much environmental noise (that occurring in the movie, not in my house) was going on. I was even thinking it would be nice if my hard-of-hearing mother could come over and watch some movies with us using the Bose system. She might be able to finally hear what was being said.

I have yet to experience the sound effects that others have reported in their reviews such as hearing sounds behind them as in a 5:1 system. We put in Harry Potter 6, a Taylor Swift live performance DVD, and watched several movies on Netflix streamed through the Roku. I still haven't heard anything similar to what a 5:1 system does. I'm not going to say, at this point, that this system won't mimick a 5:1 system since I haven't had it long enough or noodled around with it enough to know. It may very well be because of the orientation of the Bose system in our room. It really doesn't have much in the way of walls for sounds to bounce back off of. However, I will say that the clarity of sounds such as those previously unheard sounds like tiny clinking bits of glass, soft footsteps, gentle wind blowing by and the tiny sounds of insects and nature are like art to my ears. Obviously we missed those with the Sony soundbar system.

As to the price of this system. I think spending $1,500.00 on any sound system is a lot of money. But, to those of you who can afford it without any pain, and want to minimize the number of speakers and wires running to them, this is a very good option. I am not an audiophile but I know good sound when I hear it. I play and record classical guitar and strive for that pure sound, untainted by distortion. I like to be able to hear the guitarist breathing and even the sounds of the street outside while he/she is playing. So I do listen intently and am satisfied with the Bose system though the special effects have not presented themselves yet. Also, my husband will find fault and criticize almost anything beyond normal critique. He can't find anything to diss this system about. He loves it and that really surprised me as I was waiting to hear his complaints.

I haven't used the universal remote function yet on the included remote control, but will do so shortly. I doubt I will have any trouble with that but will update this review if I do. And I will update this review as I become more familiar with this system. And I have yet to determine if our Buttkicker can be connected to this system. I doubt it can at this point but I will check to be sure and report back. Overall though, it's a beautiful system not only to listen too, but it's delightful to look at as well.

UPDATE: 11.5.12
_______________
My nearly deaf mother can hear movies now while using this soundbar. Of course, it nearly deafens us if we don't wear hearing protection!
text_fidelity_b: Bose CineMate 1 SR Home Theater Speaker System (Black)

Pre-release technology reviewers commenting on the price of the Kindle Oasis are wrong. The new Kindle Oasis is worth the the price Amazon is charging, including cover it hardly represents at all an increase in price when compared with a Kindle Voyage with cover. Yet it provides the two most asked for improvements in mobile devices: increased battery life reducing the need to frequently recharge, and improved screen legibility (new sans-serif Ember font, and more LEDS that provide increased brightness).

“When we are immersed into the story of our favorite books, only that world matters.”

Pre-release technology reviewers have compared the Kindle as a single purpose e-reader, to multipurpose devices like in smartphones, tablets and computers. When we choose to read, we are seeking a bit of solitude in the day and night. Oh, how easy it is to remember being annoyed with yet another incoming phone call, text message or email. The power of focus!

“The tactile feel of a book”

Pre-release technology reviewer have labelled the Kindle as luxurious with it’s leather cover. How soon we forget our books covered with leather! And we are willing to pay an extra price for it!

As I sit across the street from the one and only Amazon retail store “in the world”, I have unboxed and set up my new Kindle Oasis. Maybe I am one of the few ordinary people outside of Amazon and the technology press in the world to have been able to purchase one so soon. The feeling reminds me of going to a release party in the same shopping center for the latest Harry Potter novel.

This Kindle is new, like the latest release from our favorite author.

It connects me to reading anywhere, late at night when there is little light.

The Kindle Oasis is magical.

NETGEAR Cable Modem CM500 - Compatible with all Cable Providers incl. Xfinity, Spectrum, Cox | For Cable Plans up to 400Mbps | DOCSIS 3.0 This is replacing a Arris Surfboard SB6141 and, so far, I've been very pleased with the performance. Set up is very simple (using Cox Cable). It did require a call to Cox to give them the ID number of the modem for activation, but the process was very quick and easy. Set up of the modem itself simply entailed plugging it in.

The modem looks as nice as a modem can look. It's pretty tip-over resistant. The indicator lights are clear without serving as a beacon when the room is dark as the Surfboard indicator lights did.

I've noticed a small increase in both download and upload speeds compared with my old DOCSYS 3.0 modem. I'm presently on a 50 mb/sec tier but will be moving to the 100 mb/sec tier later this year. That's the reason for the upgrade, since my older modem would not handle the higher speed tier very well.

The only concern I have is the operating temperature. This runs rather hot compared to the Surfboard. It does not appear to be affecting performance nor has the heat been so significant that it activated the overheat protection of the modem (the modem will shut down if it overheats and flash an error code, according to the manual). But, it does give me concern about longevity. I'll update the review down the road should reliability be a concern.

text_fidelity_a:
C2G/Cables to Go Audio Unlimited Premium Indoor/Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, Black (SPK-131U) I was very excited to have a large speaker with bluetooth capability for my Iphone to use outside by the pool. This speaker was a total dissapointment on all levels. Or maybe I just received a lemon.

I thoroughly read the instruction manual - twice - to be certain I was doing everything correctly. When I was finally able to get the bluetooth to work (after having to hold down the button on the speaker until the blue light flashed multiple times, which let me know it was activated), it did work from various locations in my yard without any failures. However, as soon as I would turn off the speaker or my Iphone - I would need to re-initialize the bluetooth as if I were logging in for the very first time. The speaker failed to remember by device and so I'd begin the pressing down of the button, blue lights flashing procedure all over again. Every single time.

So I thought I'd contact the manufacturer/vendor to see if there was anything beyond their "trouble shooting" section of the manual that I might be neglecting. I looked everywhere - the box, the manual, the speaker, everywhere - no contact information whatsoever. Not an email address, phone number, snail mail or Facebook/Twitter address to be found. You buy it - you're stuck with it. The only saving grace is Amazon if you need to return it within the acceptable time frame. But what do you do if you have a problem 6 months down the line?

I installed the batteries, tried out the a/c adapter cord, and even used the 3.5 speaker cable to attach my Iphone and by-pass the bluetooth completely. I just wanted to make sure all of these items would work. But the person who designed this unit must have been having a wonderful time when they decided that in order to plug in anything at all, you need to open the battery compartment door in order to get to the connectors. This is insane and is in no way convenient. To constantly have to remove a door, or have cords hanging needlessly is ridiculous.

The sound quality is acceptable but at the price they're selling it for, you could do far better finding a speaker that has much more to offer. And if you're looking for customer service - keep looking cause it isn't here.
text_fidelity_b: C2G/Cables to Go Audio Unlimited Premium Indoor/Outdoor Bluetooth Speaker, Black (SPK-131U)

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black Before writing this review I glanced over some reviews of earlier models, and whatever issues previous editions of the Bose SoundTouch speakers may have had seem to have been worked out with this SoundTouch 10.

Setup was simple with the SoundTouch app (available for iOS, Android, and Kindle Fire devices). We had the speaker set up and operating in less than 5 minutes using an iPad. You'll need your home network security code to connect to WiFi and that's about it.

It comes with a remote, but most of the controlling is done from your device (tablet or phone). The remote is handy for adjusting the volume when you're using your device for other things.

The speaker is about the size of a cereal box. The sound that comes out is impressive for its size. I think there's a wee bit of case resonance in the mid range, but that's just me -- everyone else thinks it sounds terrific. It doesn't rival a huge stereo system but it's really, really good.

Now excuse me while I get on my soapbox about monaural. This is a single speaker system, not stereo, and that, to me, is a good thing. I'm a fan of monaural. It solves a lot of issues about speaker placement (trying to make sure they're equally distant), and you hear the full mix as the producers and artists intended. You can move anywhere around the room and not have half the mix disappear. And if you like oldies, particularly from the 1960s, this fixes the problems caused by common pan/mix practices from that era (for example, drums and bass panned hard left, guitars and backup singers panned hard right, lead vocals in the middle). If you listen to mixes like that in headphones, you pretty much have to mix the music down in your imagination since bass/drums are exclusively in one ear and keyboards in the other. Some devices don't support mono audio output (I'm looking at you, Windows phone), and as far as I know no one makes a dual-ear mono headset for phones either. So a mono speaker solves the issue. Okay, that's it for the soapbox. Back to the review.

The only tone control available in the Bose app is bass volume. But since the sound is well engineered, it's adequate. And bass is very audible. Not subwoofer level audible, but it's very present.

The SoundTouch app itself is impressive. It really does make setup a breeze. And the listening options are VAST. Hundreds of radio stations from around the world on WiFi, streaming music services, Pandora, Spotify, and so forth. I used to do a little shortwave listening, and if you're a DXer, this exceeds the capability of SW by far, and every station is digitally clear. And you can connect directly to play music straight from your device.

Just to be clear, the speaker itself needs a wall outlet to power it. It's not battery powered. But everything else is wireless. More speakers can be added, but it's so easily unplugged and moved around that one speaker can easily be sufficient.

Nice product from Bose.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTouch 10 wireless speaker, works with Alexa - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 2 camera kit This was a real disappointment. One of the main problems is that it is only compatible with 2G and if you have a 2G and a 5G network it still may not work if your network is merged and/or you have intermittent 2G. Not sure if this applies to you? It probably does if you live in the United States in a major city. Secondly the support was terrible. Have you ever call a support line and it took 20 minutes just for them to get your name your email and whatever other information they claimed they need to identify its you? Well that's exactly the type of support you can expect from Blink. They take forever and I'm not exaggerating, forever to even get to your question which they probably won't answer because they are too busy reading from their script while they ignore your questions. Don't waste your time, your money or your very sanity. Take a hard pass on this.

Update 6/10/20:
Received an email from Alex with Amazon Executive Support. Apparently the information that we received regarding our 2g/5g internet was not valid. However using an extension cord a long one we positioned the sync module closer to our wifi modem and were finally able to set up the camera. And did get it online. However, that was all.

First of all the 2 year battery life that the description touts is just plain misleading. Apparently this camera will provide that type of battery life if you only arm the camera when you are not at home and have the settings on the lowest functionality, e.g. lowest video quality, lowest sensitivity, shortest video length etc.

Even on the highest settings we the camera just does not "CONSISTENTLY" capture video of motion or people period. Comparing this camera to our blink door bell we are getting about 10% or less video capture of motion/people. However, it does capture video when there is no apparent motion and/people in the activity zones. Also some videos are for 3 seconds or less for who knows what reason.

Not sure why Blink would think that anyone would be happy with this camera and not sure what type of situation this camera would work in since it does not do what it says it does.

This camera is a mystery and is not user friendly. Support is a joke. We have spent so much time trying to figure this camera out it is ridiculous. The Ring camera door bell is much much much easier and 100 times more reliable. We are definitely sending this back.
text_fidelity_b: Blink XT2 Outdoor/Indoor Smart Security Camera with cloud storage included, 2-way audio, 2-year battery life – 2 camera kit

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions I was so excited to finally have a separate GPS again, as my Garmin one was from 2009 (OLD maps) and using my phone was unsafe because even with stuff disabled during driving, I was still getting messages and interruptions that would pop up, plus I like listening to something on the drive, and using it as a GPS makes that tricky. Having tried several Garmin models, Apple Maps, and Google Maps, I was excited to try TomTom. And I was disappointed.

Problems:
•Screen is VERY dim in the sunlight, and living in Florida, this is most of the time. It is NOT easy to see the map, which even in my ancient Garmin is much more visible and automatically switches from day mode to night mode. Likewise, my iPhone screen automatically changes brightness for the amount of sun coming in. And this? It looks horribly dim and takes a lot of effort to see.
•Routes don’t always make sense. I’m used to some amount of this in the other systems I’ve tried, but they’re really wacky on this thing, taking a REALLY scenic route that sometimes involves making a full circle for something that was literally as easy as just turning left in the correct place.
•Point of interest search is slow and ineffective. Even with my ancient Garmin (and obviously with my phone), it would never find most places, even ones that have been there many years. This after waiting an interminable amount of time for the list to compile. Did I get the long update on my computer and add it to the GPS? Yep. I thought that was the problem, did the update, and then discovered it was Not the problem.
•Doesn’t appear to take traffic into account. Neither does my old Garmin, but it should do better than a piece of tech that’s 10 years old and at least be comparable to a current smartphone’s GPS; otherwise, what’s the point?
•Hard to stop. You want to sometimes say, “OK SHUT UP. I know the rest of the way!”, and in all other GPS systems I’ve tried, getting to the “end route/stop” place is usually two steps, max. It is long and complicated, and I don’t want to die in a car accident, so I end up having to suffer through unnecessary and often over-complicated routes that make no sense.
•Doesn’t default to turn-by-turn. Sometimes it shows an aerial view, which is zero helpful, has no detail, and requires me to think a lot about “is this to MY right or left if my car is facing this way and the map is oriented North Up and I *think* I am moving East maybe, but I can’t tell because this stupid thing is both dim and also has an unbelievably zoomed out map view where I’m not sure Where my little dot is going?!?!”

So yes. Unless I sit in the parking lot and fiddle with it for a good while, nothing is quite right, and everything takes a long time to find or set up. I tried it for a month now, and my opinion has not changed. This is frustrating.

Good things:
•nice size screen
•fun voices

Overall rating: 2 stars. I like Garmin more, and I am quite unhappy with this. It is slightly better than my now failing 10-year-old Garmin GPS. *slightly*. I would not buy this or recommend it. The interface is cumbersome, the visibility is bad in the sun, and finding places is a pain and basically 100% of the time requires me to just search for an address on my phone and plug it in. Nope.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

text_fidelity_a:
Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 THX Certified Computer Speaker System (Black) EDIT: Four-and-a-half years later I still love these speakers. They continue to sound good and functions perfectly well. I was initially worried by some reviews that stated these speakers wouldn't last but, in my case at least, they have. They get nearly daily use, some days 10+ hours, so they have held up well to fairly constant use.

I picked these up from our mail room, set them up at my desk over my lunch break, have been playing them about 15 minutes and already love them entirely. At twice the cost of my previous desktop speakers these are more than worth it.

For a few years I had a pair of relatively good [recognizable name-brand] speakers at my desk. I liked them well enough but they had one major flaw, which many people with small desktop speakers will easily recognize: when you get the volume down low (so as to not distract from work, to take a phone call, prevent an upset with others in the office, etc.) they get very flat and aren't worth listening to at all; instruments, vox, everything level off and lose their distinctness. The Klipsch 2.1 speakers sound SO much better at these lower volumes than my old speakers that I regret the years I spent with the crappy ones on my desk.

Other observations:

The first thing I noticed with these was that I had to keep the bass really low! they have a little mark on the dial which corresponds the the base level for CD/DVD which is about 30% of a full dial turn. I left it just short of that when I was tuning it by ear and only turned it up when some flatter tracks came on which needed a little boost. When a hip-hop track comes on however I am inclined to dial the bass back down just a little (apparently everything above that 30% mark is meant for gaming).

Then next thing which impressed me was the depth. The distinctness of notes and tones, the separateness between the highs and mids, etc. which these are capable of (at a regular listening volume, not quiet) leaves them sounding like actual speakers, not what you might expect from a PC/desktop speaker but what you would expect from Klipsch, even in this smaller package.

I would recommend these for anyone wanting to improve the sound out of their PC. I would also say that for a dorm or small apartment scenario these would be a fair option. The footprint on the sub only needs about 12"x10" and the satellites easily flank my dual-display setup and would work equally well on a bookshelf, coffee table, on top of a dresser, etc.

Anyone in the market for small speakers and who wants to get good sound for very little money these are a great option. If you don't want to pay $200 but you're willing to shell out $100 on lesser-quality speakers, I would suggest not wasting the $100--I wish I hadn't; now I'm out $300 and only have one pair of good speakers!
text_fidelity_b: Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 THX Certified Computer Speaker System (Black)
